title: THE NEGRO COMMUNITY: A WASTELAND OF TEARS

sense.text:
This is what belief means. “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment.” That is what belief does: it makes you take heed to God’s commandments. The black church hasn’t figured that one out yet, and doesn’t even know about the Apocrypha.

The black Christian church is confused. Sit down with a pastor and he says works and deeds can’t save him, that to inherit eternal life is only to believe on the one God sent, and that when he believes there is a nature change in his spirit man, but he doesn’t have to live it out. They lack understanding. They lack the learning to articulate exactly what the scriptures are talking about. Your spirit man changes how, like Shazam, a lightning bolt? No. Believing in the Lord shows itself in taking heed to his commandment.

And that is why Los Angeles is full of crime in the black and brown community: people are taught they are still going to be saved and all they have to do is believe. They have no works toward Christ, no charity or love toward their neighbor; they don’t even know what love is.

Now there are Christians who believe Christ is black, and some who say we’re Israelites, but they incorporate all the tenets and lies of Christianity: Christmas, Easter, Thanksgiving, and a Christ who looks like Morgan Freeman with a perm, loving everyone, all saved in Jesus if they believe. They know what we’re saying is proper, but they don’t want to upset Esau; they’re trying to stay in his good graces.

precepts.why:
The pastor kept talking about love, love, and the way they say it you’d think it’s some whoremongering homosexual thing. I don’t know what the hell they mean when they talk about love, because it ain’t what the Bible says. The Bible says: “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.”

So they never read that? If he reads it he’ll come up with, no, you don’t got to keep them. Then what does the Bible mean? They can’t answer it. The love of God is keeping his commandments, and that is what the believer takes heed to.

“And this is love, that we walk after his commandments.” That’s love. “This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.”

Walking after his commandments is what love is, and it is what belief taking heed to the commandment looks like.

“For when we were in the flesh, the motions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members to bring forth fruit unto death.” When we were in the flesh our members worked in sin. We did things by nature, natural sinful things like adultery, lying and stealing, and it brought forth fruit unto death.

“But now we are delivered from the law, that being dead wherein we were held; that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter.” The newness of spirit is the new covenant in Christ; the oldness of the letter is the covenant of animal sacrifice. When Paul talks about the law, or when we say law, they think we’re talking about animal sacrifice. If they would just take the time to listen and stop assuming what we’re talking about, things would be all right. They listen to a dumbass like Vocab Malone who don’t know a damn thing: oh, you guys want the animal sacrifice? No, we’re not. We’re talking about Christ and the keeping of the commandments.

“What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid.” Is God’s law evil? The answer is no. “Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law”: you would not know what sin is but by reading and studying the law. “For I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.” And this is why churches teach their members not to read Genesis to Malachi. They say start with Matthew, start in the middle of the book and go to Revelation, and they stay confused.

What Christ did on the cross was enough: Christ gave us grace to get ourselves together under these commandments so that we have an opportunity at eternal life. It is the law of sacrifice that doesn’t get you salvation, but all God’s commandments are morality, even the ceremonial laws, which celebrate the salvation we received in our various captivities. The feast days must still be kept. The Christian says no. Then what do you keep? During slavery the white man gave us some good holidays: Christmas, Thanksgiving, Easter, the Fourth of July. We ain’t got to keep nothing God said, but what the white man said we going to obey. That’s what these Christians do.

sense.text:
Our hope and prayer, teaching every day, morning, noon and night, is to win our people over to the Lord, and when they come into this truth they have to understand this, the women especially.

“Ah sinful nation” is talking about us. We’re the sinful nation, “a people laden with iniquity”: laden with sin, with evil works. “A seed of evildoers”: we are the seed of evildoers. “Children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.”

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”: our people revolt more and more against the Lord, and we are stricken through all the curses God put on us. “The whole head is sick”: that’s the southern kingdom, starting with Judah as the head; Benjamin is the neck and the shoulders. “And the whole heart faint.”

This is like a hospital. Everybody in here is sick. I’m sick, you’re sick, we’re all trying to get right, all battling certain problems. Brothers don’t really complain; it’s mainly the women. Everyone’s mean to me, she didn’t talk to me, she didn’t watch my kids when I asked. The letters with just complaints about sisters get chucked to the side. The one sitting next to you may be going through something. Oh God, please shut up.

I would love to say the Israelite community is the greatest community, but that can only be said of IUIC. Some congregations send donations and support us, but some brothers don’t like being told what to do, commanded and instructed in the ways of God. And there is hate every day, people who have never met us, don’t know our mama or our daddy, with so much venom against us, digging into the Bishop’s past from fifteen, sixteen years ago. Everybody in the Bible had a past, Moses, King David, all of them; the Lord forgave them and the nation moved on. No other leader in the nation of Israel is taking us to the destination we’re going to.

This is a woman who lost her child, as heavy a situation as there is, and listen to the instruction given her: “Now therefore keep thy sorrow to thyself, and bear with a good courage that which hath befallen thee.”

The amount of information coming in is great, and everybody comes in sick. We’re all trying to sort through it and get our minds right, but if you entertain everybody’s qualms about everything, you’ll never get anywhere. It’s not that it’s insensitive, though people want to portray it like we don’t care. It doesn’t mean you don’t get counsel or help, but you can’t find yourself in a circular situation trying to talk people out of certain things.

precepts.why:
Further on she is told: “And therefore shake off thy great heaviness, and put away the multitude of sorrows, that the Mighty may be merciful unto thee again, and the Highest shall give thee rest and ease from thy labour.” The Mighty is the Most High. Keep thy sorrow to thyself, shake off the heaviness, and he will be merciful again.

The scriptures are the healing. You get cured with the word of God. It’s not that we don’t care, but we can’t address everybody’s situation; you would never get through it.

sense.text: “Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save.” They made a play called Your Arms Too Short to Box with God, but the Bible says the Lord’s hand is not shortened. “Neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear”: his ear is not too heavy to hear our prayers.

Here’s the problem, why he’s not listening, not answering our prayers, not stepping in on our behalf: “But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.” That’s the problem right there. It’s not that his arm is too short or his ears too heavy. He can save you, he can deliver you when he wants, but you ain’t right. You’re not changing your life.

That’s the problem with Christianity: they’re not trying to transform their lives to that of the nation of Israel according to the holy scriptures.

This time the verse is taken slow, very slow. “Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” The unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom. You ain’t getting the kingdom. “Be not deceived”: don’t fool yourself.

“Neither fornicators”: fornicators ain’t getting in. Fornication is listed in Leviticus 18, which gives a litany, a whole list of the sexual things we are not to indulge in. A pastor who told a woman to wait on God’s time and keep silent while he went home to his wife every night; two pastors charged with child sexual abuse and child pornography, one of them enticing a fifteen-year-old boy with food and money. All that falls under fornication. You can’t make this stuff up.

“Nor idolaters”: idolatry then and now is the same thing. Back then you had Baal; now you got Mother Mary and all of that in the Catholic church, and crosses everywhere in the Christian church, crosses around their necks. In Islam a man jumps over people to kiss the black stone: idolatry on another level.

“Nor adulterers”: a bishop of Saginaw, Michigan crashed out on Facebook, admitting his own affair while exposing his wife for sleeping with his barber for three years.

“Nor effeminate”: girly boys. You might not have had a homosexual encounter, but you act very feminine. A man in women’s pants with his thing all out grabbed a microphone to sing before the church, and no man in that ministry jumped up and said no, sir; no mother came with a cloth to cover him. They’re quick to cover up the woman but not him. No standard. This is why black men leave the church. And when you bring it out, they say you’re judging. Yeah, we judging.

“Nor abusers of themselves with mankind”: homosexuals, like the pastor caught in the back seat of a car with a sixteen-year-old boy.

“Nor thieves”: northern kingdom! Get that last dollar. “Nor covetous”: a woman going after a married man, and a mother telling her the truth: you’re not stealing nobody’s husband; he knows you know he’s married with all those responsibilities and he’s still coming after you; don’t think you’re that special. You need women that’ll keep it real, not these lying hussies lying on women all the time.

“Nor drunkards”: there are different levels of drunk. Some brothers giggle, some get violent, some fall asleep, some vomit. You got to know what kind of drunk you are. The violent drunk drags his young wife around in fear.

“Nor revilers”: a reviler is someone who habitually uses harsh, abusive, insulting or slanderous language to tear down, humiliate or control others. A lot of times when people revile, they revile the word of God; they insult the prophets, they hate the prophets. Squatters living under the bridge waited until the brothers were packing up from teaching the word of God, then came cursing to make it look like they were driving them out. When we come with solutions for the black community, they revile solutions: why can’t we keep smoking weed, why can’t we sell, why can’t I sleep in the park and steal your house when you go on vacation? Because the Bible says that’s wrong. I don’t want to hear that. A man saying the slaves built nothing and thanking God for the white man; a woman pastor with a doctorate in theology who cannot answer for the scriptures that say a woman is to keep silent in the church: these are revilers. They despise the Bible.

“Nor extortioners, shall inherit the kingdom of God.” A preacher busted selling heaven dust, crushed chalk in Ziploc bags; a preacher ordering the ushers to close the doors until a thousand people give; a pastor talking about selling weed in the church. That’s a shakedown, gangsterism, anything to make a dollar. This is why we had to leave the Christian church.

“And such were some of you”: everybody in here can identify with something listed and say, I used to do that, and that, and that. Reading it cuts every one of us; this whole class is self-reflection. “But ye are washed”: washed with the word of God. “But ye are sanctified”: sanctified by the word of God in Christ. “But ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God.”

precepts.why:
The unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God, and the Bible says what righteousness is: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

So the Christian goes, oh no, that’s not the righteousness, go to Romans 10:4. We don’t run from scriptures. We explain and edify on the scriptures.

“For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.” See, we ain’t got to keep no laws, that cancels out Deuteronomy 6. No, numbskull. Christ is the end of the law of animal sacrifice for righteousness. Christ took the place of the animal sacrifice. And they think they got you with “to every one that believeth.”

Read verse one: “Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.” The whole subject is Israel being saved, and Christ is our righteousness in the law because he suffered: he took the place of the animal sacrifice, the law of sacrifice. The commandments still stand as our righteousness, and the unrighteous still shall not inherit the kingdom.

This for you porno brothers. A show of hands for who still struggles with porn, not who is always watching, but who still struggles: nine hands.

“But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.” Porn falls into that category. Looking to lust is adultery in the heart, and it stands with the fornicators and adulterers who shall not inherit the kingdom.

“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body”: the word reign means to rule. Don’t let sin rule your mortal body. Every brother says, I got the porn under control. There’s no such thing as control of sin. “That ye should obey it in the lusts thereof”: once you start obeying that lust, it has you in control. You don’t have it in control.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead.” Men and women, you are alive from the dead. We got to submit ourselves to Christ. He is our commander, our leader; what he says we must do. “And your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.”

“For sin shall not have dominion over you”: Paul is reiterating, and the word dominion goes back to reign in verse 12. Sin shall not reign in your mortal body. “For ye are not under the law, but under grace”: not under the law of sacrifice anymore, but under the grace of Christ.

“What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.” Should we keep watching porn because we’re not under the law of sacrifice but under the grace of Christ? The answer is, God forbid.

What happens when sin reigns in your body, when it has dominion over you? “And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God”: he is the guide of us who keep his commandments and precepts. “Let not your sins weigh you down”: sometimes you fall in the midst of sin and Satan whispers in your ear, you’re no good, leave this truth, the Lord can’t use a person like you. Well, he used Samson. He used David. He used a lot of our forefathers that fell to sin. “And let not your iniquities lift up themselves”: don’t let them rise back up in your body again.

“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins”: being bound in your sins goes back to sin reigning in your body and having dominion over you. A brother says, I got it in check. He’s in a store looking at porn on his phone, forgets where he is, and takes his pecker out in front of the ladies. Does that sound like he got it under control? He’s in jail. Another brother watches porn while driving home and crashes. If you’re watching porn, it has you in check. Keep a checklist in your mind and say, I’m messed up, I need help, because I could die, I could be in jail.

“And covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through”: just as no one can travel through that path, the scriptures can’t reach you no more. Your heart is hardened. Sin has dominated your life; it is ruling you; you’re not you anymore, and the scriptures have no effect on you. “It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Death, destruction: that’s your final outcome, brothers. Stop watching the porn.

sense.text:
We don’t like looking at ourselves in the mirror. Michael Jackson had a song called Man in the Mirror. “Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?” That’s the question you got to ask yourself.

We’re on the street telling the revilers the truth and they get so angry, like we just beat their mama up. We’re just reading a book, and that infuriates you so much you want to lay hands on us? And some in here, when your sin is read out, get angry as if we did something personal against you, though we don’t even know what you’re guilty of.

precepts.why:
“For my love they are my adversaries”: see what the Lord says. From the top: “Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise; For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me: they have spoken against me with a lying tongue. They compassed me about also with words of hatred”. This is the black and brown community. “And fought against me without a cause.”

We’ve never met these people, never done nothing to them, but they are furious at the word of God and want to lay hands on brothers, fight brothers. At one church they brought out a gun; another brought out the AK-47, just for reading the Bible in truth. They can hear it in the church, because they get lies in there; they know the pastor’s no damn good.

Years ago in Detroit a young man said he stopped going to a church because the pastor put the drug dealers on the books as ushers and laundered their drug money through the church, taking his cut. From the church it goes into the bank, and banks don’t ask questions. Our people are wise to do evil.

“Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee.” A scorner doesn’t want to hear the scriptures. They don’t want to hear the solutions we have according to the Bible to fix their lives. They want to hear they can still live in debauchery, that the black woman is no damn good, that they can sell drugs, beat their kids when they want or not even take care of them. That’s a destroyed mind; our people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.

“Rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.” That’s every brother and sister in here. We all got rebuked at one time or another and said, I want to learn more, I’m coming into this truth, because I know that’s the word of God. I can hear it; the spirit touched me right there.

sense.text:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge”: the knowledge it is talking about is the word of God, his laws to be specific, his laws, his commandments, his statutes. Lacking that is what has us destroyed mentally and spiritually. We are a destroyed race. The twelve tribes of Israel are destroyed as a people. And the Spanish churches do the same thing, just throwing an idol in there.

“Because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God.” It tells you right there what the knowledge is: the law of God. That’s why we are destroyed as a race, as a people, and why other races come into our communities to make the hospitals, the stores and the clinics. It isn’t that we don’t have the ability; many of us have the knowledge to do it, but they don’t want us to have the capabilities.

precepts.why:
What does “that thou shalt be no priest to me” mean? There was a promise made to us and our ancestors: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests.” A kingdom of priests.

So when Hosea says thou shalt be no priest to me, it is that promise we lost, because we forgot the law of our God.

sense.text:
“Therefore I esteem all thy precepts concerning all things to be right; and I hate every false way.” We must learn to hate every false way, and that brings us to the hair. Fake hair is a sign of trauma. People are going to get mad, and I don’t give a damn. Not alopecia or a medical condition, where sisters cover it up; we’re talking about a headful of hair that you hate. You hate your God-given hair. You won’t take the time to wash it or comb it or put grease in it.

That’s trauma in the mind of the black woman who hates her God-given hair and loves the hair of animals and of dead people on her head. The scripture says love your neighbor as yourself. Brothers, listen good: if she can’t love herself, what makes you think she can love you? This is why divorce is on the rise, why you have baby daddies and baby mamas all through the hood. She will never say out loud, I hate the way I look, but it’s hatred, it’s trauma, and she puts her trauma into her little girl.

The East Indian woman grows up feeling she’s under a curse; she shaves all her hair off and dedicates it to the gods, they tell her all her curses are in the hair, sacrifice it to the god with eight arms, then mail it to America and the UK, and the black woman puts that cursed hair on her head and wonders why she acts the way she does. Take that hair off your head. Start with that. Get your mind right.

precepts.why:
This whole class is a class of self-reflection, for all of us. “Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich? Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust”: an ostrich buries her eggs in the dust, in the sand, “And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.” She forgets exactly where the eggs are, walks all around them, steps on some and crushes them.

“She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labour is in vain without fear; Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.” God never gave the ostrich any kind of wisdom or understanding. That’s a heavy statement, because of what God compares the daughters of Zion to.

Watch what God compares the black woman to, the most educated with all the degrees: “Even the sea monsters draw out the breast, they give suck to their young ones: the daughter of my people is become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.” Cruel is mean-spirited. God through Jeremiah says the daughters of Zion are like the ostriches in the wilderness, and the ostrich is the one God gave no wisdom.

The picture fits: the fake eyelashes, the big behind, the head always moving around in everybody’s business, making noise. God knows what he’s doing. The Bible ain’t the white man’s book; the Bible is our book. And the videos going around make the black community look like a zoo, women brawling in an alley with weaves flying, narrated like a sports game. They are making black people like that the face of all black people: an ethnic image.

sense.text:
Why isn’t the Lord saving us and hearing our prayers? Our iniquities have separated us from our God. “For your hands are defiled with blood”: our hands in the black and brown community are defiled with blood. A young man in Joliet murdered his own mother, his aunt, his uncle, his brother and his three sisters; three teens robbed and killed a man; a woman who stabbed a three-year-old boy to death laughed and smiled in court. “And your fingers with iniquity”: the Bible says thou shalt not kill, and we are not taught that in church, so some of us grow up with a hateful and murderous spirit on us.

“Your lips have spoken lies, your tongue hath muttered perverseness”: like the woman bishop who says the Bible has become problematic, that its pages need to be torn out and a third testament written, that it is not the word of God but words about God. What she wants panders to homosexuals, women and crackheads.

No matter how bad, how insulting or degrading the videos are, it is filtered through the Bible, showing the stage and state of where we are today, and it is still proof that we are the children of Israel.

“None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth.” You might say our people are in the street all the time crying no justice, no peace. The justice our people want is called money. They don’t want the justice of the Bible; they’re not calling for God’s justice or pleading for God’s truth.

When our brothers and sisters are put to death unjustly, the families want the truth regarding their case, and we may march with them and support them, but they don’t want God’s truth as a whole. Do you ever see a change in any of these families? They’re still celebrating Christmas, mad at the white man while celebrating the white man’s holidays, and they want us to support them.

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall smite thee with madness.” Our people are insane. No rhyme, no reason to what they do or why they do it: that’s being smitten with madness. We have generational curses.

The man who killed his whole family had stuff going on in his head; the woman laughing in court after killing a child is stricken with madness, trauma that would take years to unfold. And still it is proof that we are the children of Israel.

Here is God’s justice: “If any man have an ear, let him hear. He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.” Now that’s justice.

And what do our people say? No, you hate the white man. They know what the scripture means: the white man is going into captivity and going to be put to death by the sword. Then they say, no, we don’t want that kind of justice; we want money, money, money.

There’s no internal change. “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.” Be transformed and changed. If I used to celebrate Christmas, I’m renewed, now I’m celebrating Hanukkah; if I used to celebrate Easter, no more, I’m celebrating Passover.

They are not being transformed, and it’s not because we’re not making an effort. They are making a conscious effort not to change: I’m not listening to you guys, I just want you to march for me and support my son or my daughter, but I’m not changing.

“Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne”: God’s throne is all about justice and judgment, and that’s what the world doesn’t want. “Mercy and truth shall go before thy face.”

The Lord is coming with justice and judgment, and the nations don’t want that. Many of them are living on stolen land, like America; this is stolen land. Oh, I can’t wait for Jesus to return. You know Jesus is about justice and judgment, right? I don’t know nothing about that. They’re lying.

Everybody says, I can’t wait until Jesus comes back. “And the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come.” All these nations, countries and religious organizations say they want the Messiah to return, but the Bible prophesies they are angry, because Christ is returning with justice and judgment. His wrath is coming. He’s not coming to hand out lollipops and hugs and kisses. “And the time of the dead, that they should be judged”: that’s our people.

“And that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great”: that reward is power. He is going to give his servants power.

“And shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth.” That’s them. They say the aerosols in the black and brown community are destroying the ozone layer, not their rockets to the moon and their missiles. They’re the ones destroying the earth, digging up and sucking out the oil that lubricates the tectonic plates, then wondering why the earthquakes are happening. They know that, and that is why they are going to be angry when he returns.

sense.text:
“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder”: the kingdom of heaven is a government. It’s not a church group. “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

Most Christians, even some Israelites, can’t explain the everlasting Father, because the everlasting Father in the Old Testament was Christ. They haven’t figured that one out. We always spoke to the Father? No, you did not speak to the Father; you spoke to Christ. That’s why he is called the everlasting Father.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end”: not a church-group government. That’s why it behooves us to learn God’s laws, his commandments and statutes. To set up a government, with everything we read at the beginning that a community consists of, God’s laws are going to filter everything for us.

When he gives his reward he is going to change the way we think. Right now we think small. I got a house: think bigger. I got property: think bigger. Like what? The world is yours. That’s too hard for me. The world is ours, and in order for the world to be ours we have to set up all kinds of things.

precepts.why:
Christ answers it himself: “Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us. Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?”

Yes, Christ looks like his Father, but what is he actually telling Philip? I created you. I’m your father, your everlasting Father; you were brought forth through me. Christ is the only begotten of the Father, which means the Father only created Christ, then told Christ, you create everything else.

In case you’re still confused, we have to shake the Christian thoughts. “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Christ was in the beginning with God, and he was God. “The same was in the beginning with God”: God is a plural text.

“All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ. That’s why he said to Philip, have I been so long time with you and you have not known me? I created all of this. That’s too heavy for a negro, because you got Baptist on your mind and Catholic in your head. It was hard for us in the beginning, but the Most High showed us.

Christ said it: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds”. A mustard seed is one of the smallest of all seeds; if you grew up in the city you don’t even know what one looks like. “But when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.” When it is grown, that is the increase of his government.

It starts small. We think we’ve got a lot, but this is small, this ain’t nothing; we are still at the mustard seed stage.

Think how the Most High uses something as small as the human mind. As a man thinketh, so is he. Every object, every invention, everything you lay your eyes on outside of the earth itself, was a thought first. We shortchange ourselves with doubt. Remove the doubt and the fear, let the Lord work on that head, and the untapped greatness waiting to bud will come forth.

“And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them: and I knew not that she was the mother of them. I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally”: Solomon learned wisdom diligently and communicated her liberally, the same thing we’re doing today. “I do not hide her riches”: we don’t hide the riches of the wisdom of God.

“For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.” If we use this wisdom, we become the friends of God. And we don’t just learn once; we’re supposed to learn daily. That’s why the classes are every day.

Now compare what God did for Solomon and us today: “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements”. You might say you know the world was made, but what elements were made to make air, or the sun? We don’t know that. Solomon understood it. “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”: he saw it all, from Adam to the second coming of Christ. “The alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons: The circuits of years, and the positions of stars”. “The natures of living creatures”: Esau puts a camera on an animal, even in its behind, trying to get on Solomon’s level with all that freakiness. “And the furies of wild beasts: the violence of winds”: tornadoes and storms. “And the reasonings of men: the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”: which herbs for what. “And all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

We’re not on Solomon’s level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, and when God opens our spirit we will be on this level and greater. That’s what the mustard seed is about: we’re starting off small and it is going to grow. This is the beginning, the mustard-seed government.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch”: that’s Christ. “And a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” See what he is going to do: execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations don’t want that. Some of us in here may not want it either, but it’s coming.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

sense.text:
Keep the thought. Verse one: his hand is not short that he can’t save us, his ear not heavy that he can’t hear our prayers. Verse two: our iniquities have separated between us and our God. Verse three: hands defiled with blood, fingers with iniquity, lips speaking lies, a tongue muttering perverseness, a female pastor wanting to rip out the testament. Put all of verses two to four together, and what comes of it? “They hatch cockatrice’ eggs”: a cockatrice is like a poisonous snake. Snake eggs. “And weave the spider’s web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth”: if you eat the eggs that come from these people, our people, you shall die. “And that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper”: the eggs are the kids that come out, little baby snakes. They produce evil followers.

Years ago at a community meeting a black woman screamed at the police for not doing their job: they’ve been selling drugs in my building for years. The police set up a sting; the drugs were being sold out of the mailboxes. They locked up two dudes: her sons. Then she came back saying it was false, with them on video. These are the snake eggs; these are the kids coming out.

“Their webs shall not become garments, neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.” Acts of violence like the brawl on the Carnival cruise ship that got passengers banned for life, and the fights breaking out at graduations, families throwing punches, someone in a cap and gown.

“Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity.” A man doing something sick and disgusting to a woman who didn’t even realize it: this is where you end up from watching porn, all you porn brothers, if you can’t break it. The demons are so heavy.

Compulsion is an uncontrollable urge or irresistible impulse to perform a specific act, often driven by an underlying obsessive thought. Pornography exacerbates those thoughts until you cannot control yourself, and you will be driven to do things like that.

As bad as all this seems, it is still proving according to the Bible that we are the people of the book. We just need help, divine intervention. “The way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings: they have made them crooked paths: whosoever goeth therein shall not know peace.” Our people have made crooked paths for themselves.

Follow the Democratic or the Republican party and you’re not going to find peace. Follow these ministers with the white Jesus over their heads and you’re not going to find peace. That cross is an idol.

“Therefore is judgment far from us”: as a result of all that we’ve read, judgment is far from us. “Neither doth justice overtake us: we wait for light”: we wait for justice, “but behold obscurity”: there’s always some confusion, something that goes wrong. “For brightness, but we walk in darkness.” It’s an unjust system. A black man was all in Esau’s face, Esau wearing the American flag proudly on his chest, so sure the young man on trial was going to get off right then, and it didn’t go that way.

We want to live filthy lives, evil, violent lives, and then expect justice from God. It don’t work like that. We do all kinds of evil and say, why isn’t God hearing us, why is he not intervening on our behalf? He told you from verse two all the way down.

“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes”: we got eyes, but we act like we ain’t got none; we act like what we just saw didn’t happen. “We stumble at noonday as in the night”: it’s high noon, but in our minds we are so spiritually blind it’s like night for us. “We are in desolate places as dead men”: our people are like the walking dead. That’s the black and brown community: desolate places.

There is a difference, though, between being spiritually slow and being spiritually dead.

“We roar all like bears”: we’re always screaming in the streets for justice, for reparations, for money. “And mourn sore like doves”: the women weeping. “We look for judgment, but there is none”: not the judgment we want. “For salvation, but it is far off from us”: because we think we get salvation the way the white man said. Say three Hail Marys and you’ll be all right; go to church every Sunday and you’re going to get it. No. Salvation is far from us.

“For our transgressions are multiplied before thee, and our sins testify against us: for our transgressions are with us; and as for our iniquities, we know them”. We know them. Our people just don’t want to be told to their face what their sins are, but they know they’re living wrong. They know they are a detriment to their own families, their own communities. You had three abortions: you are a detriment to our race. You can repent; we’re not saying you can’t.

Discussing their sins is the solution, and that is what a therapist does, except therapists start when you were five, lay you on a couch and charge you all that money. My uncle did this to me, my mother left me when I was six. You’re 42 now. You’re a grown woman, a grown man. We ain’t got all year; we get to the point: you are an adulterer, a thief, a liar, an idolater, and this is the solution to A, B and C. Therapists are doing nothing different than what we’re doing; we do it on a greater scale, with God’s word. And they go, I don’t want to hear that. Nobody wants what God says.

“In transgressing and lying against the Lord”: our people say God is white, surely he’s a white man. “And departing away from our God, speaking oppression and revolt”: that’s democracy, the flip side of the coin of Christianity. “Conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood”: lies on top of lies. A man saying Fox News should be called the Klan news, except that would dishonor the Klan because the Klan believed in Jesus; a man saying if Jesus is black heaven is a ghetto and the slaves built nothing; a man thanking every pure Jewish girl who would not lie with a black man so there would be a pure line for Mary.

“And judgment is turned away backward”: judgment is turned away from the negro and the Latino. “And justice standeth afar off”: far off from us. “For truth is fallen in the street”: no justice, no peace. “And equity cannot enter.” And now we got our heads down, sad, because we ain’t getting what we wanted.

“Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey”: if you depart from evil by repenting, you make yourself a prey. Everybody around you hates your guts now. “And the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment”: no true judgment on the earth.

precepts.why:
“But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers”. A generation of vipers: that is the same thing Isaiah was talking about. “Who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”.

You’ve got to bring forth God’s commandments in application. That proves your repentance.

Now Christ himself speaking to them: “O generation of vipers”, and that goes back to Isaiah 59. “How can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.”

Christ called them vipers, John the Baptist called them vipers, and their children are little snakes too.

“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. See what our people do: they walk after their own thoughts. They don’t give a damn what the Bible says. I do what I want to do.

And their thoughts are the white man’s thoughts. They follow the man-made religions, which don’t teach God’s laws, his commandments, his statutes: we ain’t got to keep no laws. So what do you get? Those vipers hatch eggs, and what comes out? Little vipers, little snakes. Your son, little Tyrone, is a snake, and your daughter, little Chenique, was a snake too. That’s what God is saying.

“Their webs shall not become garments.” “So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.” Their hope is cut off because they’re hypocrites, and their trust is a spider’s web: you get tangled up in that thing, and the spider comes out and bites you and eats you up.

“He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.” Your house won’t stand.

“Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me”: they look for counsel, but not from God. “And that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit”: not according to the Bible, “that they may add sin to sin”.

“That walk to go down into Egypt”: at that time it was actual Egypt, but today it’s America, spiritual Egypt. “And have not asked at my mouth”: they don’t ask the prophets what the Bible says. “To strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!” America is the shadow of Egypt. This ain’t the real Egypt, but it is the shadow of Egypt. Such a covering does not cover them; their webs do not become garments.

“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

We’re like blind people, and we got eyes. We see we’re not prospering as a people. We see we’re under constant oppression as a people. But we act like we don’t see it, because oppression has become so normal to us. It’s our everyday life.

This is what we need as a nation. We usually read it as an individual, but think of it on a bigger scale; this is not Joe or Bob, this is us. “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty”: lacking ability. “Yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate, And lifted up his head from misery; so that many that saw it marvelled at him.”

The nations are going to marvel when God raises us up. It is going to be such a shock that this low, degenerate race of people is now going to rule the earth.

Because right now we lack the ability. Black newscasters give their counsel on how countries can fix themselves while their own community is effed up; a sister who had three abortions, her house in shambles, who can’t keep a man, giving her thoughts on world events. Nobody sees the irony? Be quiet.

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver”: the great house is the nation of Israel; think of it as whatever IUIC school you come from. Every camp leader is the head of the sanctuary and must be able to identify the gold brothers and the silver brothers, the gold sisters and the silver sisters, “but also of wood and of earth”: this brother and this sister is earth, this one is wood, no damn good. If you can’t discern that, you’re going to have problems in the school, putting people in positions that don’t fit them. You are spiritually blind and destined for ruin.

Marcus Garvey put his best friends over his three ships, and they didn’t know how to run a ship. One crashed, and he lost it all, because of friend-ship. Who is best qualified for the position? Your friend might not be. Put me on the computers and I’ll mess the whole thing up; that ain’t my gift. A school leader who doesn’t study, and all hell breaks loose out there.

“And some to honour, and some to dishonour.” Some brothers and sisters are just slow and need a little more time to acclimate and grow into certain things; don’t put them in that position yet if others are better qualified.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use”. Purge yourself from the wood and earth spirits. They see this truth not as a government, not as the mustard seed of a government, but as a social club, a Buena Vista Social Club: dancing every new moon, but when it comes to doing God’s work, they’re confused.

“He that believeth on him is not condemned”: if you believe on the black Messiah, you are not condemned. “But he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God”: you ain’t even keeping commandment one.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world”: Christ is that light that came into the world. “And men loved darkness rather than light”: sin rather than Christ and keeping the commandments, “because their deeds were evil.” From Isaiah to John it’s saying the same thing.

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.” They hate Christ. They hate keeping the laws, they hate the commandments, because if you come to Christ your deeds will be reproved: thou shalt have no other gods before me, thou shalt not bow down to any graven image, remember the sabbath day to keep it holy, honor thy father and thy mother, thou shalt not kill. They don’t want to hear that.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” We want Christ, the word of God, to make our deeds manifest: Lord, show me.

It’s saying the same thing Isaiah 59:15 is saying: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.” That includes some of your mothers and fathers too, sisters and brothers.

Depart from evil and you make yourself a prey to the ones who hate him that rebukes.

sense.text: A man on a clip says the Hebrew Israelites care more about the complexion of their Jesus than his words, and quotes the verse to say Christ calls all: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” What Edom is doing now is hiring black people, dumb Africans, to use Zionist talking points against the truth. We didn’t say it; a black man said it. He doesn’t know what the hell he’s talking about.

precepts.why:
Isaiah answers it: “And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”. Rest from what? From the hard bondage: that’s slavery, wherein we were made to serve.

The rest Christ gives is the rest promised to the people put under hard bondage. The man on the screen doesn’t know what is going on.

precepts.ref: Song of the Three Holy Children 1:1-6
precepts.why:
This is when the three Hebrew brothers were cast into the fire by Nebuchadnezzar: “And they walked in the midst of the fire, praising God, and blessing the Lord.” Babylon destroyed the temple, and all the princes in the king’s house were made eunuchs, these brothers included.

“Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers: thy name is worthy to be praised and glorified for evermore: For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us”. Imagine being cast into the fire and saying, thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us. “Yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.” “In all the things that thou hast brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, even Jerusalem, thou hast executed true judgment”: we deserve what we got. “For according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins.”

They understood that thing. Our people today have a hard time understanding it. “For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee.” The hard bondage is the true judgment for our sins.

So we are messed up as a people, which is why God says he will yet choose us: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel”. Because of the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: I know you’re not in your right minds yet, but I will yet choose you. That’s mercy. Thank God for mercy, because we need that mercy, man. We are crazy.

Think about how messed up our minds are, and the Most High is still going to have mercy on us. “How is the gold become dim! how is the most fine gold changed! the stones of the sanctuary are poured out in the top of every street. The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, how are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!”

At one time we were compared to stones and jewels, a golden cup. Today we’re the earthen pitchers. One has value; one does not.

“And yet for all that, when they be in the land of their enemies”: like today, here in America. “I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”: he ain’t going to destroy us utterly, “and to break my covenant with them: for I am the Lord their God.”

“But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors, whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the heathen, that I might be their God”. Who said bloodline ain’t important? The Bible says, I will remember the covenant of your ancestors.

Saying the same thing in the New Testament: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of salvation is Christ; he’s the King.

“As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”: the same thing Leviticus 26 is saying. “To perform the mercy promised to our fathers”, our ancestors, “and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham, That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”.

Ask the Christians who know about the split between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom: where is the northern kingdom in the New Testament? They don’t know. “For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”. They’re mentioned here, the northern kingdom and the kingdom of Judah; in Paul’s other epistles he uses different words.

“Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days”: Israel as a collective. “I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”.

A famous scripture that all the churches use but don’t understand: “If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways”. Turn means repent. “Then will I hear from heaven”.

Remember, his ear is not heavy that he can’t hear, but our iniquities have separated us from our God. Now he has given us the solution: humble ourselves, pray, seek his face and turn from our wicked ways, and then he will hear from heaven, “and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.”

“The Lord killeth, and maketh alive”: it’s the Lord who allows death throughout the world, and life in this earth. “He bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich”: who did you think made us poor? “He bringeth low, and lifteth up.”

“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust”: the poor he lifts out of the dust is you and me, us. “And lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill”: why is the Holy Spirit on Hannah calling us beggars? Because we’re the ones always begging: for reparations, for a job, for social services, for food stamps, going to another race of people and not to our own, because our own people are ill. We effed up; we ain’t got our minds right, and the system is set up to keep us down. Wherever we live is a dunghill, not only Haiti; America too. We came from ruling the planet, the gold, the diamonds and the pearls, and look at us now: our minds ain’t right, our clothes ain’t right, our houses thrown up out of sheetrock overnight.

“To set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory”: planet rulership, domination. “For the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.”

sense.text: “And he saw that there was no man”: no man to bring truth and justice, “and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his arm brought salvation unto him”. His arm is Christ: remember, sit down at my right hand. Christ is the right arm. “And his righteousness, it sustained him.”

“For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head”: Christ put on righteousness as a breastplate and a helmet of salvation; this goes back to Ephesians 6. “And he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing”: he ain’t coming back for love and handshakes. “And was clad with zeal as a cloke”: as a cape.

“According to their deeds, accordingly he will repay, fury to his adversaries, recompence to his enemies; to the islands he will repay recompence.” Not only is he going to repay the other nations; unrepentant Israelites will get the same judgment.

“So shall they fear the name of the Lord from the west”: we’re in the west, brothers, the western hemisphere; it says so prophetically. “And his glory from the rising of the sun”: the eastern hemisphere, where our people live also. “When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the Lord shall lift up a standard against him”: he is only going to allow Esau to do but so much.

“And the Redeemer shall come to Zion”: Christ is coming to Israel. “And unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the Lord”: not all nations. See who he is coming for. Why is he saying that? Because from verse two down to verse fifteen he listed all our wicked deeds.

“As for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the Lord; My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth”: he’s talking to Isaiah, “shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed’s seed”: not just Isaiah, the rest of us, “saith the Lord, from henceforth and for ever.” Twelve tribes.

We definitely needed those commandments. Corinthians lists a whole lot of sins and then says such were some of you, and that is the black community. Christianity wants us to forget God’s commandments and tries to confuse it to say we’re about animal sacrifices; we’re not, but you have to keep the commandments.

The black community is the city, and it is the kingdom. We have to learn how to apply God’s commandments now, and that’s how we build that city. If we don’t get rid of the sin, we can never be that proper city the Lord is trying to build, where your light shines: “Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.”

The only way the Most High is going to deal with the city of righteousness is when we keep God’s commandments. It is the commandments that identify whether I’m a thief, a fornicator, a liar, a covetous man, effeminate, all that we read in Corinthians; the law, the commandments of God, have to expose those demons. That’s how we become that righteous city, think like that mustard seed and grow into great righteousness. Sin has to be brought out and exposed, and repentance has to come forth. These churches got to learn that.

Men, we want dominion, rulership; we want to subdue the nations. The government must be in place, and in that we must be keeping the commandments. It’s the only way we’re going to get it. Christ is black, God is black, and we’re made after his image. “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion”: dominion is rulership.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.” Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything underfoot.

At that time everybody was of color, but he gave a specific people rulership. So when you read likeness, understand it’s more than just what you look like.

precepts.why:
“As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is not just what you look like. It’s being righteous. And in being righteous we will subdue, we will have dominion over things. That government cannot happen unless we’re righteous.
